classes.note: Counted per region: each regional council election counts once. The 15 ordinary-statute regions' elections since 1970 come from the Interior Ministry's historical archive (Eligendo). Sicily, Sardinia, Aosta Valley, Trentino-Alto Adige, and Friuli-Venezia Giulia elect their councils under their own statutes, and Eligendo doesn't list them; of these, only the Aosta Valley elections since 2003, from the region's own results pages, are counted so far. Neither are four ordinary-statute elections that Eligendo leaves out: Marche in 2020 and 2025 and Molise in 2018 and 2023. The five special-statute regions first voted between 1947 (Sicily) and 1964 (Friuli-Venezia Giulia), the fifteen ordinary ones on 7 June 1970. Trentino-Alto Adige's council has since 2001 been the two provincial councils sitting together, counted under the autonomous provinces. Systems: PR by province (1970-1990), the Tatarellum's PR plus a regional list bonus (1995-), and each region's own law since the 1999 constitutional reform.

classes.name: Consiglio comunale
classes.finest_note: comune; polling section in recent Eligendo files
classes.note: Every comune elects its council for five years (four from 1993 to 1999) on one Sunday of the ordinary round between 15 April and 15 June, or the next year's round after an early dissolution, so each comune keeps its own cycle and about a fifth vote each year. Comuni up to 15,000 inhabitants: a single round, two-thirds of the seats to the winning mayor's list; larger ones: a majority bonus to the mayor's coalition. Sicily, Sardinia, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Trentino-Alto Adige, and the Aosta Valley run their own municipal elections. Dated rows from 1989 count the comuni in Eligendo's files for each year (the ministry's archive holds every date from 1989 but only the general rounds of 1964, 1970, 1975, 1980, and 1985 before it, so earlier years are expected from the statutory cycle); the ministry's files cover the ordinary-statute regions and Sardinia, and Sicily, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Trentino-Alto Adige, and the Aosta Valley only in some years. Where a regional list gives a count (Friuli-Venezia Giulia from 1998, Sicily from 2008, and the Aosta Valley and Trentino-Alto Adige in most years), the row uses it for that region in place of Eligendo's, and its note names the figures; Friuli-Venezia Giulia 1993-1997, Sicily 1993-2007, and the uncertain Trentino-Alto Adige years keep Eligendo's partial count or none.

classes.name: Sindaco
classes.note: Elected directly with the council since Law 81/1993 (before, by the council). Comuni up to 15,000 inhabitants: one round by plurality, a tie going to a runoff (TUEL art. 71); above 15,000: absolute majority, else a runoff between the top two on the second Sunday after (art. 72). Sicily and the other special-statute regions set their own thresholds. Dated rows from 1993 count the comuni in Eligendo's files for each year; the ministry's files cover the ordinary-statute regions and Sardinia, and Sicily, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Trentino-Alto Adige, and the Aosta Valley only in some years. Where a regional list gives a count (Friuli-Venezia Giulia from 1998, Sicily from 2008, and the Aosta Valley and Trentino-Alto Adige in most years), the row uses it for that region in place of Eligendo's, and its note names the figures; Friuli-Venezia Giulia 1993-1997, Sicily 1993-2007, and the uncertain Trentino-Alto Adige years keep Eligendo's partial count or none.

cadence.runoff_rule: Comuni above 15,000 inhabitants: a runoff between the top two on the second Sunday after the first round when nobody wins an absolute majority; smaller comuni elect by plurality.

classes.name: Consigli e presidenti di municipio e di circoscrizione
classes.note: Comuni above 250,000 inhabitants, and every metropolitan capital, must divide into districts (TUEL art. 17): Rome's 15 municipi, Milan's 9, Naples' 10, Turin's 8 circoscrizioni, Genoa's 9 municipi, Bologna's 6 quartieri, Florence's 5, Venice's 6 municipalità, and others. Their councils and presidents are elected with the city council; smaller comuni abolished theirs in 2010.

classes.name: Referendum comunali
classes.note: Consultative, abrogative, or proposing referendums each comune may hold under its statute (TUEL art. 8), such as Rome's 2018 referendum on its transit company; held on the municipality's own schedule and published only by the comune.

classes.name: Referendum per il distacco di comuni (art. 132 Cost.)
classes.name_en: Referendums on moving municipalities between regions
classes.note: State-run referendums in the comuni asking to leave one region for another (Constitution art. 132, Law 352/1970 arts. 42-45), such as the Valmarecchia comuni in 2006 and Sappada in 2008; a majority of the electorate must approve, then Parliament decides.

cadence.administered_by: Ministero dell'Interno; the Corte di cassazione's central office

classes.name: Elezioni primarie
classes.disposition_reason: Primaries (the center-left's since 2005, for prime minister, party leader, mayors, and regional presidents) are organized and counted by the parties; no public body administers or certifies them.

classes.name: Consiglio superiore della magistratura
classes.disposition_reason: Two-thirds of its members are elected by the magistrates (a professional ballot) and one-third by Parliament in joint session (Constitution art. 104); neither is a popular election.

classes.name: Consorzi di bonifica
classes.disposition_reason: Their assemblies are elected by the landowners who pay the consortium's levies, voting by contribution class in ballots each consortium runs; they are not public elections.
